contexts.text: Preface. By Moses and Elias (at the Transfiguration), there was represented the Word of the Old Testament... By Elias the prophet, all the Prophets. AC 2606:end.
By Elijah, and Elisha is represented the Lord as to the Word.

As... Elijah represented the Word itself, and also John, who is therefore called Elias who was to come, in order that they might represent the Word such as it is in the external form, that is, in the letter, Elijah was girt with a girdle of skin at his loins...
By Elijah was represented the Lord.
Under Elisha, see this reference.

Elias represents the Word... This is meant by... There were many widows in the days of Elias... yet to none of them was Elias sent except into Sarepta of Sidon... ()... The widows who were within the vastated Church, to whom Elias was not sent = those who are not in truth because not in good.
By Elijah and by Elisha was represented the Lord as to the Word, thus by them was represented the Word; specifically, the prophetic Word. AC 5321:5. AC 5922:5. AC 9372:end. AC 9995:3.
The Lord is represented by... many in the Word... By Elijah is represented the Lord as to the prophetic Word.

There are especially two who represent the Lord as to the Word, namely, Moses and Elijah; Moses, the Lord as to the historical books; Elijah, as to the Prophets. There are besides Elisha, and lastly John the Baptist, wherefore the latter is he who is meant by Elias who was to come. AC 7643:end.
They were carried by horses of fire, as Elijah was.
To none of them was Elias sent = the Lord as to the Word, thus the Word of the Lord, not sent to others, because not received anywhere else.
In the Word there are many who represent the Lord as to truth Divine, or as to the Word, but the chief among these are Moses, Elijah, Elisha, and John the Baptist.

That Elias had come, and that they had not acknowledged him, but had done to him whatsoever they would () = that the Word had indeed taught them that the Lord would come, but that they did not want to comprehend it, interpreting it in favour of self- dominion, and thus extinguishing the Divine that is in it.
As John the Baptist represented the Lord as to the Word, when he was speaking about the Lord, who was the Word itself, he said that he was not Elias.

The reason Elijah and Elisha were called the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof, is that each represented the Lord as to the Word; and by a chariot is signified doctrine from the Word; and by horsemen, intelligence.
By Moses and Elias was represented the historical and prophetical Word... AE 64:2. AE 594:2. AE 624:22. AE 937:5. AE 1070:3.
In the Word in Heaven... instead of Elijah, there is the prophetical Word.
By Jezebel's wanting to kill Elijah, is signified their wanting to destroy the Word. AE 160:2.
As Elijah and Elisha represented the Lord as to the Word, and thence signified doctrine from the Word, as all the prophets did, they are called the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof.
As Elijah represented the Lord as to the Word, which is the doctrine of truth itself; and as a mantle = Divine truth in general, which is the Word in ultimates, the mantle of Elijah came to Elisha.

As by Elijah and Elisha was represented the Lord as to the Word, in which are all truths from good, when this representation was transferred from Elijah to Elisha, which is signified by his casting his mantle upon him, Elisha was seen ploughing with twelve yoke, and himself between the twelfth; by which is signified the formation of the Church by means of truths from good from the Word.

Hence the prophets of the Old Testament represented the Lord as to the doctrine of Divine truth; and the chief of them represented the Lord as to the Word itself from which is the doctrine of Divine truth; as Moses, Elijah, Elisha, and John the Baptist.
That Elijah represented the Lord as to the Word, is evident from the miracles performed by him; by all of which are signified such things as are of Divine truth or the Word.
Not that he was Elias, but that he had a like representation to Elias; namely, the Word.
By Elijah the prophet () is meant John the Baptist, because by him in like manner as by Elijah is represented the Word.
